subject: Request: latest vulnerability assessment (hosted API) & secure transfer options
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@greenbridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: latest vulnerability assessment for Redwood hosted API and secure delivery

Hi Alex,

Hope you're well. Greenbridge's InfoSec team is updating our vendor evidence pack and we need the latest vulnerability assessment / penetration test summary for Redwood's hosted API environment. Specifically we need:
- Executive summary and scope (external vs internal, authenticated tests)
- High/critical findings and current remediation status
- Any customer-impacting CVEs identified since Jan 2026

For transfer, we prefer one of these secure options: short-lived pre-signed S3 link, temporary SFTP account with IP allowlist, or an encrypted archive where the key is exchanged out-of-band. We also need confirmation that the report will be redacted of any customer PII and production tenant identifiers.

Can you confirm availability and the preferred secure transfer method? We are on a tight compliance timeline—would appreciate ETA by EOD Thursday if possible.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
Senior Security Manager
Greenbridge Health Tech
[Attachment: greenbridge_vendor_checklist.xlsx]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@greenbridge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest vulnerability assessment for Redwood hosted API and secure delivery

Hi Liam — thanks for the note and the checklist. We're able to share a redacted vulnerability assessment (executive summary + full findings matrix) that meets SOC 2 / SIG evidence needs. A couple quick clarifications so we pack exactly what you need:

1) Scope: do you require internal network testing artifacts (host-level logs) or just the application/API assessment + exploit narratives?
2) Redaction: we'll remove customer tenant IDs and PII by default. If you need additional redaction (IP-range masking, service account names), let us know.
3) Transfer method: we can do either
   - Pre-signed S3 (48h expiry, server-side encryption),
   - Short-lived SFTP account with explicit expiry and IP allowlist, or
   - Encrypted ZIP (7z/AES-256) and we share the passphrase over a different channel.

Naomi/Dev — I requested the latest artifacts and remediation matrix. Dev, can you confirm which transfer option is simplest for ops and whether we can produce an S3 presigned link scoped to a single object with 24–48h TTL? Also, flag any items that still contain customer data so we can redact.

Liam — if you can confirm scope and preferred transfer option I’ll get this moving. We should be able to deliver the redacted package within 2 business days once transfer method is confirmed.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@greenbridge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest vulnerability assessment for Redwood hosted API and secure delivery

Hey all — quick technical notes on transfer options and redaction process: 

- Pre-signed S3: We can upload the package to an internal S3 bucket and create a pre-signed GET with configurable TTL. Default TTL we can do is 24 hours; if you need 48h we can request it. Objects will be SSE-S3 encrypted. We will provide an object checksum (SHA256) so you can validate integrity.

- SFTP: We can spin up a temporary SFTP user limited to a single directory, with an expiry timestamp on the account. We can also apply IP allowlisting if you provide the source IP(s) (or Greenbridge CIDR). This is auditable in our IAM logs.

- Encrypted archive: We'll create a 7z archive with AES-256, send the archive over email or S3, and share the passphrase via an alternate channel (Signal or phone). Note: internal policy prefers pre-signed S3 for traceability.

Redaction workflow: Naomi will run the auto-redaction script that strips tenant IDs and any obvious customer email addresses; then we do a manual pass for contextual redaction. Any artifacts flagged as "sensitive" (DB dumps, full auth logs) will be excluded from the package and we can provide a redacted executive summary instead.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm transfer method (Liam)
2) If SFTP chosen, provide IP(s) for allowlist; if you prefer cross-account S3, provide an ARN/assume-role details.
3) We'll stage the package and send a checksum + brief transfer runbook.

ETA: once transfer method confirmed, package ready in ~24 business hours; redaction edge cases may add time.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: transfer_runbook_v1.md (stub)]

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@greenbridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, security@greenbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-21T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest vulnerability assessment for Redwood hosted API and secure delivery

Thanks — Greenbridge would prefer the pre-signed S3 option with 24h TTL. We can provide an AWS role ARN to allow Redwood to write directly into a temporary bucket (cross-account PUT) if that's easier; otherwise presigned GET to your uploaded object is fine.

Scope: we need the application/API assessment and findings matrix (including exploit steps), but we do not require raw logs or DB dumps. Please redact tenant IDs and PII as discussed. If you can deliver the redacted package to S3 by EOD Friday (Greenbridge time) that meets our timeline.

Confirming: 24h pre-signed GET, redacted package, include remediation_matrix_v1.xlsx and SHA256 checksum.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — please send ETA and the presigned link when ready.

Best regards,
Liam
Senior Security Manager
Greenbridge Health Tech
[Attachment: greenbridge_acct_details.txt]
